title: SYSK Selects: How Labor Unions Work
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of a 2011-era episode on how labor unions work, reposted in April 2020 with a political-season intro. The hosts open with banter about Wisconsin's 2011 Scott Walker legislation that stripped state employee unions of collective bargaining, and public opinion on unions. They trace unions from medieval trade guilds through 19th-century industrial strikes (Triangle Shirtwaist fire, Haymarket affair and May Day origins, Pinkerton agents), then cover union basics: bargaining units, collective bargaining agreements, dues, local chapters, and benefits and wage statistics. They discuss criticisms of unions, the National Labor Relations Act and NLRB, Taft-Hartley (including the secondary boycott ban and the Reagan air traffic controller firings), the Landrum-Griffin-style Labor Management Reporting and Disclosure Act, union decline since the 1970s and income inequality, the AFL-CIO, the Teamsters and Jimmy Hoffa. The episode ends with a listener mail about DonorsChoose.org and off-topic banter about Joe Garden and craftwork.
topics: Labor Management Reporting and Disclosure Act

segments.title: Rerun intro and Wisconsin union fight
segments.summary: Josh introduces this Selects rerun from May 2012 as political season begins. The hosts banter, then discuss the 2011 Wisconsin legislation under Governor Scott Walker that stripped state employee unions of collective bargaining and required pension and benefit concessions, plus Pew polling on public views of organized labor.

segments.title: Origins: trade guilds and the Industrial Revolution
segments.summary: The hosts trace union roots to medieval trade guilds that shared techniques and pushed for better prices and wages. They move to the 19th-century Industrial Revolution, factory conditions, child and women's labor, and the Triangle Shirtwaist fire as a turning point.

segments.title: Violent 19th-century strikes and Haymarket
segments.summary: The hosts describe violent strikes of the 1800s, with National Guard, police and Pinkerton agents confronting workers. They cover the Haymarket affair in Chicago, the convictions and executions, the pardons, and how May Day and Labor Day observances developed, including Grover Cleveland moving the US Labor Day holiday to September.

segments.title: Basics: bargaining units, CBAs, dues and democracy
segments.summary: The hosts explain how workers form a bargaining unit with elected leaders to negotiate with employers, and how a collective bargaining agreement (CBA) is signed and enforced through grievances and arbitration. They discuss the give-and-take balance, union dues (around fifty dollars a month as cited), and union democracy in theory.

segments.title: Local unions and benefits statistics
segments.summary: The hosts explain local unions as chapters of national organizations, using film industry crews as an example. They cite Department of Labor figures on median weekly income, health, dental and vision coverage, and wage gaps for women, African Americans and Latinos between union and non-union workers.

segments.title: Union protections and criticisms
segments.summary: The hosts discuss protection from unjust firing, using the Florida case of workers fired for wearing orange as an example, and right-to-work or at-will employment. They then cover criticisms: protecting poor performers, harm to competitiveness, and state employee pension costs. They note Eisenhower's praise of unions and unions' role in civil rights legislation.

segments.title: Union decline, NLRA, Taft-Hartley and LMRDA
segments.summary: The hosts cover union membership decline from its mid-century peak to about 11.8 percent, with private sector under seven percent, and a study by Bruce Western and Jake Rosenfeld linking union decline to income inequality. They describe the National Labor Relations Act and NLRB, the Ford Harry Bennett goon squad, the Taft-Hartley Act (including the secondary boycott ban and Reagan firing air traffic controllers), and the Labor Management Reporting and Disclosure Act addressing corruption and mob influence.
topics: Labor Management Reporting and Disclosure Act

segments.title: AFL-CIO, Teamsters and Jimmy Hoffa
segments.summary: The hosts describe the AFL-CIO federation and its founder Samuel Gompers, mention the Teamsters, and discuss Jimmy Hoffa's disappearance and mob ties and his son James P. Hoffa leading the Teamsters today.
